chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz Al-Abdi, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Cheese and walnuts, when they are combined, in each one of them is a healing, and if they are separated, in each one of them is an illness.'
ai.seo_question: What is the health benefit of combining cheese and walnuts according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the principle of *tadafu'* (mutual interaction) in dietary medicine, illustrating how the combination of cheese and walnuts creates a synergistic healing effect that is absent when consumed separately. This reflects the broader Shia scholarly tradition of integrating practical health advice with spiritual and physical well-being, emphasizing that the context of consumption can transform a substance from beneficial to harmful.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdul Aziz Al Abdy who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The cheese and the walnuts, when they gather together, in each one of them is a healing, and if these are separated, in each one of these is an illness’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from ‘Abd ‘Abd al-’Aziz al-‘Abdiy who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘When cheese and walnut come together in each of them there is a cure but separately each one has an illness with it.’”
